summary.en: Salvadoran forces are searching for four soldiers missing after a gang ambush near Port-au-Prince, while Benin has pledged 2,000 troops to assist in the fight against gangs. President Bukele has deployed 2,000 Salvadoran troops to Haiti and denied accusations that his forces carried out airstrikes. The United Nations reports 193 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP. The postponed presidential election is now scheduled for July 2027, and hunger is worsening as high food prices and El Niño persist.
summary.nb: Salvadoranske styrker leter etter fire soldater som er savnet etter et gjengoverfall nær Port-au-Prince, mens Benin har lovet 2 000 soldater for å bistå i kampen mot gjenger. President Bukele har sendt 2 000 salvadoranske soldater til Haiti og avvist påstander om at hans styrker utførte luftangrep. FN rapporterer 193 dødsfall i kamper i 2024, ifølge UCDP. Det utsatte presidentvalget er nå planlagt til juli 2027, og sulten forverres ettersom høye matpriser og El Niño vedvarer.

background.title: Haitian conflict
background.extract: Since 2020, Haiti's capital Port-au-Prince has been the site of an ongoing armed conflict between rival gangs and the state. The government of Haiti and national security forces have struggled to maintain their control of Port-au-Prince amid this conflict, with gangs speculated to control up to 90% of the city by 2023. In response to the escalating fighting, an armed vigilante movement, known as bwa kale, also emerged, with the purpose of fighting the gangs. On 2 October 2023, United Nations Security Council Resolution 2699 was approved, authorizing a Kenya-led "multinational security support mission" to Haiti. Until 2024, the war was between two major groups and their allies: the Revolutionary Forces of the G9 Family and Allies and the G-Pèp. However, in February 2024 the two rival groups united in a coalition known as Viv Ansanm, formed to oppose the government and the UN mission.
